newsitem.title: CANADA: Forest fire threatens northern Ontario town.
newsitem.headline: Forest fire threatens northern Ontario town.

text.p: A forest fire that threatened this small northeastern Ontario city on Thursday was expected to stabilise overnight, authorities said.
About 500 people were evacuated as the fire approached within five miles (8 km) of the town centre.

"It looked as if the wind was going to push it right toward the city and then all of a sudden it shifted in a different direction," Tom Steepe, a local television reporter, told Reuters. "Things are stable now, but everyone is on standby."
Officials said the winds were expected to calm overnight.
No injuries were reported. Those evacuated from two trailer parks and homes near the fire were expected to spend the night in community centres.

Vic Power, mayor of this mining, timber and paper-making town, declared a state of emergency on Thursday afternoon, but told the populace that everything was being done to protect residents' lives and homes.

About 100 firefighters were on the scene, along with about 30 personnel form the Ministry of Natural Resources. Fire crews were using water-bombing aircraft to attempt to douse the flames, which witnesses said appeared to be about 50 feet (15 metres) high in some spots and jumping from treetop to treetop.
